title: POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade without targetTier returns 400 INVALID_TIER
preconditions: Org has pricing_v1 feature flag enabled
Valid JWT with billing.update permission
steps: Call POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade with an empty body (no targetTier)
expectedResult: 400 response with errorCode/body indicating INVALID_TIER; no SubscriptionOrg document is modified.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade no longer exists; plan changes are now submitted as SubscriptionRequest documents via POST /v1/subscriptions/requests. See BILL-INT-010.

title: Upgrading to an enterprise/contact_sales tier returns requires_contact instead of processing a Stripe change
description: Enterprise-tier or ctaType==='contact_sales' targets are not self-serve; the endpoint short-circuits to a CTA response rather than calling Stripe. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no requires_contact/Stripe branch in the new request-based flow; ctaType='contact_sales' on a SubscriptionPlan now only changes the displayed price label, and every plan change (including 'enterprise') is submitted as an identical SubscriptionRequest for admin/MSSP review.
preconditions: Org currently on 'scale' tier
Target plan 'enterprise' has ctaType='contact_sales'
steps: Call POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade with targetTier='enterprise'
expectedResult: 200 { status:'requires_contact', requiresContact:true, csmEmail:'sales@vibrantix.ai', hubspotFormUrl:<string> }. No Stripe subscription-update call is made and the org's tier is unchanged.

title: Upgrade is blocked with 409 DOWNGRADE_PENDING when a scheduled downgrade already exists
preconditions: Org has an active pending-tier-change document (a downgrade scheduled for the next renewsAt)
steps: Call POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade with a valid targetTier while the pending downgrade is still active
expectedResult: 409 { code:'DOWNGRADE_PENDING', message:'Cancel pending downgrade before upgrading' }. Caller must call DELETE /v1/billing/plan/pending-change first.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the pending-tier-change document and its 409 DOWNGRADE_PENDING response no longer exist; request.service.js's submit() has no check that blocks a new plan_change request while a downgrade request is pending. Flagged as an unverified gap — see BILL-INT-010.

title: Downgrading from the enterprise tier is rejected and points to a different CSM email than the upgrade-to-enterprise path
description: Enterprise downgrade requires talking to a CSM. Worth pinning: the downgrade-blocked email (csm@vibrantix.ai) differs from the upgrade-to-enterprise email (sales@vibrantix.ai) — verify this isn't an accidental inconsistency before it ships to more customers. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no enterprise-tier downgrade block or CSM-contact branch anywhere in request.service.js; every tier's downgrade is now an identical SubscriptionRequest requiring admin/MSSP approval.
preconditions: Org currently on 'enterprise' tier
steps: Call POST /v1/billing/plan/downgrade with targetTier='scale'
expectedResult: 409 { code:'DOWNGRADE_NOT_ALLOWED', message:'Enterprise downgrades require contacting your CSM', details:{ requiresContact:true, csmEmail:'csm@vibrantix.ai' } }.

title: Downgrade with usage over the target tier's caps requires acknowledgeOverCap=true or returns 422
preconditions: Org usage: 12 users, target 'growth' tier limits.users=10
steps: Call POST /v1/billing/plan/downgrade with targetTier='growth' and no acknowledgeOverCap field
Repeat the same call with acknowledgeOverCap=true
expectedResult: First call: 422 { code:'OVER_CAP_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED', message:'Usage exceeds limits of target tier. Set acknowledgeOverCap=true to proceed.', details:{ overCap:{ users:true, ... } } }. Second call: 200/scheduled success — a pending-tier-change is created for the next renewsAt.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — acknowledgeOverCap and the 422 OVER_CAP_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED response no longer exist anywhere in the codebase; no equivalent usage-vs-target-limit check was found in the V2 downgrade request path. This was a P0 case pre-rewrite — see the gap-fill case BILL-INT-016.

title: Cancelling a pending downgrade when none exists returns NO_PENDING_CHANGE rather than a generic error
preconditions: Org has no active pending-tier-change document
steps: Call DELETE /v1/billing/plan/pending-change
expectedResult: Response carries code 'NO_PENDING_CHANGE'; no error is thrown and no side effects occur. Confirms the client's existing 'treat as no-op' handling matches server intent.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — DELETE /v1/billing/plan/pending-change and its NO_PENDING_CHANGE response no longer exist; the client's cancelPendingChange() now resolves the pending request client-side from GET /v1/subscriptions/requests before ever calling the server. See BILL-SAN-007 for the resulting dead-code finding in PendingDowngradeBanner.jsx.

title: GET /v1/billing/invoices returns an empty paginated shape for an org with no Stripe customer yet
preconditions: Org has no billing.stripeCustomerId set
steps: Call GET /v1/billing/invoices
expectedResult: 200 { items:[], page:1, pageSize:25, total:0, nextCursor:null } — no 4xx/5xx thrown for the common 'never billed yet' state.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — GET /v1/billing/invoices and the entire invoice-history feature were deleted; there is no Stripe, no invoice collection, and no invoices endpoint anywhere in the current codebase (MSSP's getClientBilling hardcodes invoices: []).

title: All customer-facing /v1/billing/* routes 404 when pricing_v1 is disabled for the org
description: isPricingV1Enabled(orgId) gates the whole customer billing API (env PRICING_V1 or per-org PRICING_V1_ORG_ALLOWLIST). Public plans/tiers catalog and the Stripe webhook are exempt. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the pricing_v1 feature flag and isPricingV1Enabled() no longer exist; the V2 subscriptions API has no equivalent per-org flag gating.
preconditions: Org is not in PRICING_V1_ORG_ALLOWLIST and PRICING_V1 env flag is off
steps: Call GET /v1/billing/plan, GET /v1/billing/usage, and POST /v1/billing/plan/upgrade for the flagged-off org
expectedResult: Each call returns 404 { error:{ code:'NOT_FOUND', message:'Not found' } }. GET /v1/billing/public-plans (or plans-catalog public variant) and POST /webhooks/stripe remain reachable regardless of the flag.

title: billingProjectAccess middleware requires and validates projectId for project-billed organizations
description: billing.routes.js (lines ~56-67) enforces projectId presence and project-org ownership for orgs on the project scope of billing. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — billingProjectAccess middleware no longer exists; subscription.routes.js uses requireProjectMembership({required:false}) instead, and project-ownership validation now only happens inside request.service.js's validateSubject() for POST /requests, not on the GET read endpoints. See BILL-INT-015 and BILL-SEC-009 for re-verification under the new model.
preconditions: Org's billing scope is 'project' (project_billing_v1 enabled)
steps: Call a project-scoped billing endpoint (e.g. GET /v1/billing/plan) with no projectId query param
Repeat with a projectId belonging to a different organization
expectedResult: First call: 400 'projectId is required for project-billed organizations'. Second call: 404 'Project not found'.

title: POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with type='plan_change' for a non-MSSP org always routes to route:'admin' and leaves entitlements untouched until approved
description: Replaces the deleted instant self-serve upgrade: request.service.js's routeFor() sends every customer-submitted request to 'admin' unless an active MsspClientRelationship with customerSelfRequestEnabled exists. There is no more self-serve, immediate plan change of any kind.
preconditions: Org has no active MsspClientRelationship
Valid JWT with billing.update permission
A valid target planId from /v1/subscriptions/catalog
steps: Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with { type:'plan_change', requestedItems:[{planId}], effectivePolicy:'immediate' } and an Idempotency-Key header
Inspect the created SubscriptionRequest's route/status fields
Call GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current and confirm the plan/entitlements are unchanged
expectedResult: 201 response with route:'admin', status:'submitted'. GET /current still reflects the pre-request plan/entitlements — nothing is applied until an admin (or authorized MSSP) approves the request.

title: Submitting a subscription request without an Idempotency-Key header is rejected, and replaying the same key returns the original request unchanged
preconditions: Valid JWT with billing.update permission
steps: Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with a valid body but no Idempotency-Key header
Repeat the call with the same Idempotency-Key header and the same body twice in a row
expectedResult: First call: 400 'Idempotency-Key is required'. The two identical-key calls: the second returns the exact same SubscriptionRequest document (same requestNumber/_id) as the first — no duplicate SubscriptionRequest is created for orgId+idempotencyKey.

title: An actor cannot approve, reject, or mark needs-info on their own submitted subscription request
description: request.service.js's review() throws 422 SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED whenever requestedByType/requestedBy match the deciding actor's type/id — this applies uniformly to admin, mssp, and (structurally) any future customer-decision path.
preconditions: An admin user submitted a SubscriptionRequest on behalf of an org (requestedByType='admin', requestedBy=<adminId>)
steps: As that same admin user, call POST /api/admin/subscription-requests/:requestId/approve
expectedResult: 422 { errorCode:'SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED' }; the request's status remains 'submitted' and no entitlement changes are applied.

title: Approving a term_end-effective request leaves status='approved' without applying it until desiredEffectiveAt has passed
description: review()'s apply() call is only triggered immediately when `!request.desiredEffectiveAt || request.desiredEffectiveAt <= new Date()`. A term_end downgrade/framework-removal approved today with a desiredEffectiveAt next year must NOT touch the SubscriptionInstance until the subscription-term.worker picks it up at the right time.
preconditions: A submitted 'downgrade' request with effectivePolicy='term_end' and desiredEffectiveAt = current term's termEnd (in the future)
steps: Approve the request via POST /api/admin/subscription-requests/:requestId/approve
Immediately call GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current for the org
Fast-forward (or wait for) the subscription-term worker's tick past desiredEffectiveAt and re-check
expectedResult: Immediately after approval: request.status='approved', appliedInstanceId is still null, and GET /current still shows the pre-downgrade plan. After the term worker's tick past desiredEffectiveAt: request.status='applied', appliedAt is set, and GET /current reflects the new (downgraded) plan and entitlements.

title: GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current returns 404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_CONFIGURED for an org with no SubscriptionInstance yet
preconditions: A freshly created org with no initial_subscription request ever applied
steps: Call GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current for the new org
expectedResult: 404 { error:{ code:'SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_CONFIGURED' } } — not a 500 or an empty-but-200 shape. The client's SubscriptionRequests.jsx treats exactly this status+code pair as the 'needs an initial_subscription request' state.

title: Submitting a subscription request with a projectId belonging to a different organization is rejected 404
description: request.service.js's validateSubject() checks Project.exists({_id:projectId, organizationId:orgId, isActive:true}) before anything else in submit(). Direct successor to the deleted billingProjectAccess middleware, but now scoped only to the write path (POST /requests), not the GET reads.
preconditions: Two orgs A and B, each with at least one active project
Valid JWT for an org-A billing.update user
steps: As the org-A user, call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with projectId set to an org-B-owned project's _id
expectedResult: 404 'Project not found'. No SubscriptionRequest document is created.

title: A downgrade request is accepted and applied even when current usage exceeds the target plan's entitlement limits — no over-cap acknowledgement gate was found
description: The pre-rewrite acknowledgeOverCap/422 OVER_CAP_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED safeguard (previously P0, BILL-INT-005) has no equivalent anywhere in request.service.js's validateItems()/review()/apply() for type='downgrade'. This case documents current behavior as a real gap pending confirmation from product/eng, in the same spirit as BILL-UNIT-007's tierCode gap.
preconditions: Org's current usage: 12 active users; target plan's 'users.active' entitlement = 10
steps: Submit a 'downgrade' SubscriptionRequest targeting the lower-capacity plan
Approve and let it apply at term end (or force-apply for the test)
Inspect the resulting EntitlementBalance for 'users.active' and the org's actual active-user count post-apply
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request applies successfully with no 422/warning of any kind — the new EntitlementBalance.limitValue is set below the org's actual usage (12 users against a limit of 10), silently putting the org over its own new cap with no acknowledged-overage flow and no read-only/lockout mechanism observed to follow automatically. Flag as a gap versus the deleted V1 safeguard rather than assuming a defect until confirmed with the over-limit copy in components/billing/OverLimitBanner.jsx, which implies an over-limit state is expected to exist somewhere but its trigger condition was not found in this request path.

title: Immediate grandfathering (PATCH .../plans/:id with grandfatheringMode='immediate') carries forward already-consumed ai.credits usage onto the new plan version without zeroing it
description: Regression guard for the incident admin.controller.js's _applyGrandfatheringImmediate() comments describe as confirmed in production on 2026-08-07 — a race let $setOnInsert lose the carried usedValue for 3 orgs. The fix makes the carry an explicit unconditional $set after syncInstance() runs.
preconditions: An org on plan version 1 with EntitlementBalance 'ai.credits' usedValue=3400 for the current term
Admin updates that plan with grandfatheringMode='immediate'
steps: PATCH /api/admin/billing/plans/:id with a benign field change and grandfatheringMode='immediate'
Immediately read the affected org's EntitlementBalance for 'ai.credits' on its new (version 2) SubscriptionInstance
expectedResult: The new instance's 'ai.credits' EntitlementBalance shows usedValue=3400 (and the same reservedValue as before), never reset to 0 — regardless of any race between syncInstance()'s $setOnInsert carry and the controller's explicit follow-up $set.
